seed_id: topic:Reducing incorrect answers in RAG systems by detecting contradictions between retrieved documents and allowing the model to abstain when evidence is insufficient.

idea.title: Mitigating RAG Hallucinations via Contradiction-Aware Abstention and Evidence Entailment Verification
idea.research_problem: Large Language Models relying on Retrieval-Augmented Generation frequently hallucinate or generate ungrounded responses when confronted with conflicting or insufficient evidence passages, failing to abstain appropriately when contextually contradictory data is retrieved.
idea.research_gap: Bounded search findings indicate that while existing work addresses chunk-free retrieval and contrastive explanations for RAG, current frameworks lack a lightweight inference-time verification mechanism that explicitly detects inter-document contradictions and triggers calibrated model abstention when evidence does not logically entail the answer.
idea.methodology: We propose a two-stage inference framework combining text entailment transformation and contradiction detection. First, we adopt a frozen encoder with a lightweight learned query transformer to align retrieval embeddings for semantic entailment. Second, we introduce a structured verification module that decomposes retrieved passages into atomic facts, checks for pairwise contradictions, and evaluates logical entailment against the query. If inter-document contradictions exceed a threshold or entailment scores fall below a calibrated confidence margin, the system forces the generator to abstain rather than hallucinate an answer.
idea.expected_contribution: We hypothesize that explicitly modeling inter-document contradictions and coupling them with a calibrated abstention gate will significantly reduce factual hallucination rates in open-domain QA while preserving answer recall on supported queries.
idea.experimental_setup: We evaluate on open-domain question answering benchmarks including HotpotQA and subset derivations from REVEAL, using a consumer GPU (12 GB VRAM) for local inference and embedding transformations. We benchmark our pipeline against standard vanilla RAG and contrastive retrieval baselines.
idea.evaluation_strategy: We measure Exact Match (EM), F1 score, and specifically Abstention Precision/Recall to quantify whether the model correctly abstains on contradictory or insufficient contexts without refusing answerable queries.
feasibility_assumptions: A consumer GPU with 12 GB VRAM is sufficient to run local inference for small-scale open-source LLMs and embedding transformations without full model retraining.
Publicly available datasets like HotpotQA and REVEAL provide adequate multi-document instances containing conflicting or noisy evidence passages.
search_queries: contradiction detection in retrieval augmented generation
abstention mechanisms for faithful question answering

assumption_checks.assumption: The lightweight query transformation model can be optimized within local hardware constraints without full LLM fine-tuning.
assumption_checks.validation_step: Train the projection MLP using frozen encoder outputs on a small subset of HotpotQA for 5 epochs and measure gradient stability.
assumption_checks.acceptance_criterion: Training completes within 4 hours on a 12 GB GPU with validation loss decreasing monotonically.
assumption_checks.fallback: Substitute the learned MLP with a fixed rule-based query expansion heuristic.

assumption_checks.assumption: Prompt-based atomic fact decomposition and contradiction detection can run reliably on a 7B parameter open-weights model.
assumption_checks.validation_step: Run the 4-step factual decomposition pipeline on a 200-sample validation split and compute agreement with human contradiction labels.
assumption_checks.acceptance_criterion: Achieves at least 65 percent agreement with reference contradiction tags.
assumption_checks.fallback: Use stricter regex parsing filters combined with external NLI entailment classifiers.

prior_work_comparison.shared_mechanism: Utilizes a transform model to align query embeddings for semantic entailment without re-encoding the corpus.
prior_work_comparison.proposed_difference: Integrates transform retrieval directly with an explicit inter-document contradiction detector and a calibrated abstention gate, rather than focusing solely on entailment matching.
prior_work_comparison.verification_needed: Ablate the transform retrieval component to measure its isolated impact on contradiction detection accuracy.

prior_work_comparison.shared_mechanism: Constructs contrastive explanations or comparative passages to improve reasoning in RAG.
prior_work_comparison.proposed_difference: Focuses on automated contradiction detection and programmatic abstention rather than generating qualitative contrastive text demonstrations.
prior_work_comparison.verification_needed: Compare output refusal accuracy against contrastive prompt demonstrations on ambiguous datasets.

prior_work_comparison.shared_mechanism: Evaluates reasoning chains for attribution to evidence passages and logical consistency.
prior_work_comparison.proposed_difference: Applies verification at the retrieved evidence and contradiction-checking stage prior to generation rather than evaluating completed reasoning chains post-hoc.
prior_work_comparison.verification_needed: Evaluate runtime overhead and error propagation differences between pre-generation filtering and post-hoc verification.

idea.title: Mitigating RAG Hallucinations via Contradiction-Aware Abstention and Evidence Entailment Verification
idea.research_problem: Large Language Models relying on Retrieval-Augmented Generation frequently hallucinate or generate ungrounded responses when confronted with conflicting or insufficient evidence passages, failing to abstain appropriately when contextually contradictory data is retrieved.
idea.research_gap: Bounded search findings indicate that while existing work addresses transform-based textual entailment retrieval and atomic fact state tracking separately, current frameworks lack an integrated, resource-constrained inference-time verification mechanism that explicitly detects inter-document contradictions and triggers calibrated model abstention when evidence does not logically entail the answer.
idea.methodology: We propose a two-stage inference framework combining a lightweight query transform for semantic alignment and a structured verification module. First, we adopt a frozen encoder with a lightweight learned query transformer to align retrieval embeddings for semantic entailment. Second, rather than exhaustive multi-step decomposition, we introduce a lightweight cross-encoder NLI scoring module and a contradiction gate to evaluate pairwise passage consistency and logical entailment against the query. If inter-document contradictions exceed a calibrated threshold or entailment scores fall below a confidence margin, the system forces generator abstention. We implement 4-bit INT quantization via bitsandbytes to ensure execution within a 12 GB VRAM limit.
idea.expected_contribution: We hypothesize that explicitly modeling inter-document contradictions via a lightweight cross-encoder coupled with a calibrated abstention gate will significantly reduce factual hallucination rates in open-domain QA while preserving answer recall on supported queries.
idea.experimental_setup: We evaluate on open-domain question answering benchmarks including HotpotQA and subset derivations from REVEAL, using a single consumer GPU (12 GB VRAM) running a 7B open-weights model with 4-bit quantization. We benchmark our pipeline against standard vanilla RAG, contrastive retrieval baselines, and a sequence-level log-probability abstention baseline.
idea.evaluation_strategy: We measure Exact Match (EM), F1 score, and specifically Abstention Precision/Recall to quantify whether the model correctly abstains on contradictory or insufficient contexts without refusing answerable queries.
feasibility_assumptions: A 7B parameter open-weights model with 4-bit INT quantization can execute local inference and embedding transformations within 12 GB VRAM.
Publicly available datasets like HotpotQA provide adequate multi-document instances containing conflicting or noisy evidence passages.

assumption_checks.assumption: The 7B parameter quantized model paired with the cross-encoder verification module fits within the 12GB VRAM constraint during batch inference.
assumption_checks.validation_step: Run memory profiling over a 50-sample validation batch from HotpotQA while tracking peak VRAM consumption.
assumption_checks.acceptance_criterion: Peak VRAM usage remains strictly under 11.5 GB.
assumption_checks.fallback: Reduce the batch size to 1 and offload auxiliary layers to CPU.

assumption_checks.assumption: A lightweight cross-encoder NLI classifier correlates reliably with contradiction presence without full prompt-based atomic decomposition.
assumption_checks.validation_step: Compute classification agreement between the cross-encoder and human-annotated contradiction labels on 200 validation samples.
assumption_checks.acceptance_criterion: Achieves at least 65 percent agreement with reference contradiction tags.
assumption_checks.fallback: Incorporate a stricter regex parsing filter combined with verbalized confidence thresholds.
